title: The symbol of a one dimensional module is the product of the symbols of its minimal prime quotients raised to the local multiplicities
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a finite module M of dimension one over a Noetherian local ring A and nonzerodivisors a, b on M, the lemma computes the symbol d_M(a, b) as the product over the minimal primes q_i of the support of M of d_{A/q_i}(a, b) raised to length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) (statement lines 17576-17591). The proof is an induction along a filtration rather than a direct computation: it takes a filtration 0 = M_0 in M_1 in ... in M_n = M whose successive quotients are A/p_j for primes p_j, uses that each p_j is either one of the minimal primes q_i of the support or the maximal ideal, and shows that for a fixed i the number of j with p_j = q_i equals the length of M at q_i (proof lines 17594-17606). The recurrence is then read off from the two structural lemmas: when p_j is a minimal prime the symbol multiplies by d_{A/q_i}(a, b), and when p_j is the maximal ideal the symbol is unchanged (proof lines 17607-17620). Setting up the filtration so that the multiplicities appear as the number of occurrences of each minimal prime is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
